newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil markets quiet, negative tone persists.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil markets quiet, negative tone persists.

text.p: NWE fuel oil markets were quiet on Thursday morning with sentiment negative, traders said.
High sulphur barge trade started very slowly with a little business heard done just before lunch. Offers were $82 fob, with prompt bids at $80 and further out at $81.
Utilities were holding down offers with the $75 cif number floated on Wednesday still in the market, though sellers had not come down that far.
Rumours persisted that high sulphur material may head from Europe or the Mediterranean to the Far East, with a 50kt purchase from Italy of end-April barrels by a German trader said headed to Asia.
The German was heard to have bought on Wednesday at high quotes plus either 25 cents or $1.
A cargo of low sulphur straight-run was heard traded from Belgium to Mediterranean coast France at $93.50 fob on Wednesday, helping that grade to recover from Tuesday's weak numbers.
An E-4 from Klaipeda, loading around April 20th, was believed to have changed hands but the buyer and price was not immediately known.
